alt: A sorted array with a write pointer and a read pointer. write only advances, and copies the current value into its own slot, when read finds a value that differs from what write already holds. Slots at or before write are done; the read pointer scans ahead of it.

steps.caption: write starts at index 0, holding arr[0] = 1. read starts one slot ahead.
arr[1] = 1 repeats the value write already holds (1). read moves on without writing.
arr[2] = 2 is new, it does not match arr[write] = 1. write advances to index 1 and stores 2.
arr[3] = 2 repeats the value write already holds (2). read moves on without writing.
arr[4] = 3 is new, it does not match arr[write] = 2. write advances to index 2 and stores 3.
read has reached the end. The first 3 slots hold the unique values: [1, 2, 3].
write starts at index 0, holding arr[0] = 4. read starts one slot ahead.
arr[1] = 4 repeats the value write already holds (4). read moves on without writing.
arr[2] = 4 repeats the value write already holds (4). read moves on without writing.
arr[3] = 4 repeats the value write already holds (4). read moves on without writing.
read has reached the end. The first 1 slots hold the unique values: [4].
